criteria.description: Identify the user's primary sport or activity
Understand the user's main goal (e.g. race prep, general fitness, strength gain)
Find out if there's a target event, race, or competition date
Any specific performance targets (time, distance, weight, etc.)
Assess the user's experience level with their sport
Their current fitness level and recent training load. Based on this answer, suggest workout intensity and volume
How many days per week the user can commit to training
Specific days they prefer to train or need to rest

What equipment specific for their sport does the user have access to. Ask this only when the sport needs very specific equipment and the user clearly mentioned that they are a beginner or just starting out.
Access to sport-specific facilities (pool, track, climbing gym, fitness gym, etc.)
Whether to include strength and conditioning sessions. Ask only when the user is creating a program for a sport that does not include this implicitly.
Whether to include dedicated stretching and mobility work. Do not treat these as a separate workout DAY while planning the program, these are always complementary to a rest day or after a workout.
Other activities to include (yoga, pilates, swimming for recovery, etc.)
Any current injuries or physical limitations
Past injuries that tend to flare up during training
